description: The Product Tours page (TourCatalog) enables users to generate AI-powered interactive product tours from existing UI Bridge page specs. Users select one or more page specs, choose a target audience (new user, power user, or evaluator), then trigger AI generation via the runner's /ai/prompt endpoint. Generated tours are previewed as TourCard components before being persisted to instanceStorage. Saved tours are cataloged by audience category and can be played back with the floating TourPlayer modal, or exported as JSON, Markdown, or HTML. The page implements a multi-phase generation workflow: idle → generating → previewing → done (or error on failure). Tour steps reference registered UI elements by ID and can execute demo actions (click, type, select, navigate) that the player performs automatically.

groups.name: Page Structure
groups.description: Core layout and headings that establish the page identity. The page is a flex column with a fixed header and a scrollable content area. The main heading and section heading must be present for the page to be considered loaded.

assertions.description: A 'Product Tours' heading (h2) is present at the top of the page
A 'Generate New Tours' section heading (h3) is present in the page content area
The root element of the page has data-page-id='product-tours', allowing UI Bridge to identify the page

The page is structured as a full-height flex column with a fixed header section and a scrollable content area. The header contains the 'Product Tours' heading (and optionally a Reset button). The content area contains the spec selector, audience selector, action buttons, status messages, preview cards, and the saved tours catalog — all scrollable as a single column.

groups.name: Page Spec Selector
groups.description: Multi-select control that lists all discovered UI Bridge spec files (*.spec.uibridge.json). Users select which pages to generate tours from. Includes a 'Select all' / 'Deselect all' toggle. Specs are discovered via import.meta.glob at build time.

assertions.description: A 'Select Pages' label is visible above the spec list
A 'Select all' toggle button is present when no specs are selected (or when not all are selected). When all specs are selected, the same button reads 'Deselect all'.
assertions.precondition: At least one spec file exists and not all specs are selected

assertions.description: When no spec files are discovered, the spec list area shows 'No specs found' in muted text
assertions.precondition: No *.spec.uibridge.json files exist in the specs directory

assertions.description: Clicking a spec item in the list toggles its selection state. A selected spec shows a CheckSquare icon and an accent background (bg-accent/30). An unselected spec shows a Square icon with no background. The 'Generate Tour' button becomes enabled once at least one spec is selected.
assertions.precondition: At least one spec file exists in the spec list

groups.name: Target Audience Selector
groups.description: A select dropdown that determines the persona the AI uses when generating tour content. Three audiences are available: new-user, power-user, and evaluator. The selected audience also controls how saved tours are grouped and labeled in the catalog.

assertions.description: A 'Target Audience' label is visible above the audience dropdown
The audience dropdown contains the option 'New User — basics & common workflows'
The audience dropdown contains the option 'Power User — advanced features'
The audience dropdown contains the option 'Evaluator — differentiators & ROI'

groups.name: Generation Action Controls
groups.description: The action buttons in the generation workflow change based on the current phase. In idle/error/done phases the 'Generate Tour(s)' button is shown. In the previewing phase, 'Save' and 'Regenerate' buttons replace it. A 'Reset' button appears in the header whenever the phase is not idle.

assertions.description: A 'Generate Tour' button (with Sparkles icon) is present in the idle phase
assertions.precondition: Page is in idle phase

assertions.description: The 'Generate Tour' button is visually disabled (opacity-50, not interactive) when no specs are selected. Clicking it should not trigger generation. Once at least one spec is selected, the button becomes active.
assertions.precondition: Page is in idle phase

assertions.description: When multiple specs are selected, the button label reads 'Generate Tours' (plural). When exactly one spec is selected, it reads 'Generate Tour' (singular).
assertions.precondition: Page is in idle phase and spec list has at least two items

assertions.description: During the previewing phase, a 'Save N Tour(s)' button with a Download icon is visible and styled in green (text-green-600). N reflects the count of generated tours. Clicking it persists all previewed tours to instanceStorage under the key 'qontinui-product-tours'.
assertions.precondition: Page is in previewing phase

assertions.description: During the previewing phase, a 'Regenerate' button with a RefreshCw icon is visible alongside the Save button. Clicking it re-triggers the AI generation with the same specs and audience selection, replacing the current preview with new results.
assertions.precondition: Page is in previewing phase

assertions.description: A 'Reset' button with a RefreshCw icon is visible in the page header whenever the phase is not 'idle'. Clicking it returns the page to the idle phase, clearing all generated preview tours and status messages.
assertions.precondition: Page is in any phase other than idle (generating, previewing, done, or error)

groups.name: Generation Status Messages
groups.description: Contextual status indicators appear below the action buttons during active phases. The generating phase shows a spinner and loading text. The error phase shows an error message in a red-bordered box. The done phase shows a success message in green. These messages are mutually exclusive.

assertions.description: During the generating phase, a Loader2 spinner is visible alongside the text 'Generating tour(s) with AI...' in muted foreground color. The action buttons are not clickable while this state is active.
assertions.precondition: Page is in generating phase (AI request is in flight)

assertions.description: During the error phase, an error message is displayed in a red-themed box (bg-red-500/10, border-red-500/20) with an AlertCircle icon. The message contains the actual error text returned from the API. The 'Generate Tour' button is still visible so the user can retry.
assertions.precondition: Page is in error phase (AI generation failed)

assertions.description: After saving tours, the page enters the done phase and displays a success message in green (text-green-400) containing the count of saved tours, e.g. '2 tour(s) saved'. The Generate Tour button is also visible to allow creating additional tours.
assertions.precondition: Page is in done phase (tours were just saved)

groups.name: Generated Tours Preview
groups.description: When AI generation completes, the page enters the previewing phase and displays a 'Preview' heading above a grid of TourCard components — one per generated tour. Users review these before deciding to save or regenerate.

assertions.description: A 'Preview' heading (text-xs font-medium, muted-foreground) is visible above the tour cards during the previewing phase
assertions.precondition: Page is in previewing phase

assertions.description: One TourCard is rendered for each generated tour in the preview. Each card displays the tour's title, subtitle, audience badge, metadata row (estimated minutes, step count, page count), and a 'Start Tour' button. The cards are displayed in a grid layout.

target.label: Start Tour button on preview card

assertions.precondition: Page is in previewing phase and at least one tour was generated

assertions.description: The number of TourCard components in the preview grid should equal the number of specs that were selected for generation (one tour generated per spec). If 3 specs were selected, 3 tour cards should appear. A mismatch indicates that some tours failed to generate silently.
assertions.precondition: Page is in previewing phase

groups.name: Saved Tours Catalog
groups.description: The lower section of the page displays all previously saved tours, separated from the generation controls by a divider. Tours are grouped by audience type with labeled category headings. This section only appears when at least one tour has been saved to instanceStorage.

assertions.description: A 'Saved Tours' heading (h3, text-sm font-medium) is visible below the generation section divider when at least one tour has been saved
assertions.precondition: At least one tour has been saved to instanceStorage

assertions.description: Tours with targetAudience 'new-user' are grouped under the heading 'Getting Started' (text-xs, uppercase, tracking-wide)
assertions.precondition: At least one saved tour has targetAudience 'new-user'

assertions.description: Tours with targetAudience 'power-user' are grouped under the heading 'Power Features'
assertions.precondition: At least one saved tour has targetAudience 'power-user'

assertions.description: Tours with targetAudience 'evaluator' are grouped under the heading 'Product Overview'
assertions.precondition: At least one saved tour has targetAudience 'evaluator'

assertions.description: Each TourCard in the saved tours section has a 'Remove' button that appears on hover (opacity-0 → opacity-100 transition). Clicking Remove deletes that specific tour from instanceStorage and removes its card from the catalog immediately. The audience group heading is hidden if its last tour is removed. If all tours are removed, the entire 'Saved Tours' section disappears.
assertions.precondition: At least one tour is in the saved tours catalog

assertions.description: The saved tours catalog is loaded from instanceStorage on page mount using the key 'qontinui-product-tours'. Tours persist across page navigations and app restarts. After saving new tours or removing tours, the catalog reflects the current storage state without requiring a page refresh.
assertions.precondition: At least one tour has been saved

groups.name: Tour Card Component
groups.description: TourCard renders the metadata and actions for a single ProductTour. It appears in both the preview grid and the saved tours catalog. The card layout includes a header (title, subtitle, badge), a metadata row, and action buttons.

assertions.description: Each TourCard displays the tour's title (text-sm font-semibold, truncated with ellipsis if long)
assertions.precondition: At least one TourCard is rendered

assertions.description: Each TourCard displays an audience badge with color coding: new-user is green, power-user is blue, evaluator is amber. The badge text reflects the audience value (e.g., 'new-user', 'power-user', 'evaluator').
assertions.precondition: At least one TourCard is rendered

assertions.description: Each TourCard displays a metadata row with three items: estimated duration (Clock icon + 'N min'), step count (Layers icon + 'N steps'), and page count (User icon + 'N page(s)'). All values are derived from the ProductTour data object.
assertions.precondition: At least one TourCard is rendered

assertions.description: Each TourCard has a 'Start Tour' button (primary style, Play icon). Clicking it sets the active tour and opens the TourPlayer modal overlay without navigating away from the current page.
assertions.precondition: At least one TourCard is rendered

assertions.description: In the saved tours catalog, each TourCard displays three export buttons: 'HTML', 'JSON', and 'MD'. Clicking each triggers a file download in the corresponding format. The filename follows the pattern '{tour.id}.{ext}'.
assertions.precondition: At least one tour is in the saved tours catalog

groups.name: Tour Player Modal
groups.description: TourPlayer is a fixed-position floating card (bottom-right, z-[9998]) that overlays the current page while playing a tour. It displays one step at a time, executes demo actions automatically, and provides Back/Next navigation. It does not navigate away — the product tours page remains visible behind it.

assertions.description: Clicking 'Start Tour' on any TourCard causes the TourPlayer card to appear in the bottom-right corner of the screen (position: fixed, bottom-6 right-6). The card is 384px wide (w-96) and slides in from the bottom.
assertions.precondition: A tour has been launched by clicking 'Start Tour'

assertions.description: The player displays the current step's headline (h3, text-base font-semibold) and body text (p, text-sm, muted-foreground). The tour title appears in smaller text above the headline. The step content changes when the user clicks Next or Back.
assertions.precondition: TourPlayer is open and playing

assertions.description: The player footer shows progress dots: the current step dot is wider (w-4) and uses primary color; completed step dots are small (w-1.5) and use primary/50 opacity; upcoming step dots are small and use muted-foreground/30 opacity. The dot pattern visually communicates position within the tour.
assertions.precondition: TourPlayer is open and playing

assertions.description: Clicking 'Next' advances to the next step. On the last step, the Next button label changes to 'Finish' — clicking it transitions to the done screen showing 'Tour Complete'. The 'Back' button (ChevronLeft) is only visible when currentStepIndex > 0 and navigates to the previous step. These are the only navigation controls; there is no step indicator the user can click directly.
assertions.precondition: TourPlayer is open and playing with at least two steps

assertions.description: When a step has a demoAction defined and the player is executing it, a 'Demonstrating...' indicator appears (Loader2 spinner + text-xs text-primary). Demo actions include: clicking an element by ID, typing text, selecting a dropdown value, navigating to a page URL, or waiting a specified number of milliseconds.
assertions.precondition: TourPlayer is playing a step with a demoAction and the action is executing

assertions.description: After clicking 'Finish' on the last step, the player transitions to a done screen showing a 'Tour Complete' heading (h3, text-lg font-semibold) and the tour's subtitle. If the tour has a CTA object, a CTA button is shown with the CTA label; clicking it opens cta.url in a new tab (if provided) or fires the CTA action. A 'Close' button (text-xs, muted-foreground) dismisses the player.
assertions.precondition: TourPlayer has reached the last step and Finish was clicked

assertions.description: When a step has a targetElement with an elementId, the player locates the DOM element using the selector [data-element-id='{elementId}'] and applies a CSS class based on the highlight type: 'tutorial-target-active' (spotlight), 'tutorial-target-pulse' (pulse), or 'tutorial-target-border' (glow). The element is scrolled into view with smooth behavior. The highlight class is removed when the step changes.
assertions.precondition: TourPlayer is playing a step with a targetElement that has a valid elementId

groups.name: AI Tour Generation Output Quality
groups.description: The AI generation process is the core domain logic of this page. It sends a structured prompt containing the spec's assertion data, the page's registered UI elements, and an audience context to the /ai/prompt endpoint. The output must conform to the ProductTour schema and meet specific quality criteria. These assertions define what 'correct' AI output looks like.

assertions.description: Each generated tour should contain between 5 and 8 steps (ProductTourStep[]). Fewer than 5 steps is too sparse to cover the page meaningfully. More than 8 steps is too long and risks losing user engagement. The step count is visible on each TourCard in the metadata row (e.g., '6 steps').

target.label: Step count in tour card metadata

assertions.precondition: Page is in previewing phase and at least one tour was generated

assertions.description: The generated tour's targetAudience field must match the audience selected in the dropdown. The audience badge on the TourCard displays this value. A new-user tour should cover basics and common workflows. A power-user tour should focus on advanced features. An evaluator tour should emphasize differentiators and ROI. Audience mismatch (e.g., power-user content in a new-user tour) indicates a prompt construction bug.
assertions.precondition: Page is in previewing phase and tours were generated

assertions.description: Any step that specifies a targetElement must reference an elementId that exists in the registered UI elements list fetched from /ui-bridge/control/elements. Steps referencing nonexistent element IDs will cause TourPlayer to silently skip highlights, degrading the tour experience. Validate by checking that each elementId in step.targetElement appears in the element list that was fetched before generation.
assertions.precondition: Page is in previewing phase and tours were generated

assertions.description: Step headlines should be benefit-focused, not feature-name labels. Examples of correct headlines: 'See your automation in action', 'Build complex workflows in minutes'. Examples of incorrect headlines: 'Workflow Builder', 'Settings Panel', 'Click the button'. The AI is instructed to avoid feature-name-only headlines. This is visible in the TourPlayer and in the preview TourCards.

target.label: Step headline in TourPlayer or preview

assertions.precondition: Page is in previewing phase or TourPlayer is open

assertions.description: Steps with demoAction type 'type' should use realistic example values in their value field (e.g., 'My Automation Workflow', 'user@example.com') rather than placeholder strings like 'test', 'foo', 'bar', or 'example'. Placeholder strings are visible if TourPlayer executes a type action on a visible input. The AI is explicitly instructed to use realistic demo data.
assertions.precondition: TourPlayer is playing a step with a type demoAction

groups.name: Tour Export
groups.description: Tours in the saved catalog can be exported in three formats: JSON (raw data), Markdown (human-readable documentation), and HTML (standalone dark-themed self-contained page). All exports trigger a browser file download using an ObjectURL blob.

assertions.description: Clicking the 'JSON' export button on a saved TourCard downloads a file named '{tour.id}.json' containing a pretty-printed JSON representation of the ProductTour object with 2-space indentation. The JSON includes all fields: id, title, subtitle, targetAudience, estimatedMinutes, pages, steps, and optional cta.
assertions.precondition: At least one tour is in the saved tours catalog

assertions.description: Clicking 'MD' export downloads '{tour.id}.md' containing: a title heading, subtitle as a blockquote, a metadata line (Audience | Duration | Pages), numbered step list with headline and body, demo action descriptions, and an optional CTA section. The file is text/markdown MIME type.
assertions.precondition: At least one tour is in the saved tours catalog

assertions.description: Clicking 'HTML' export downloads '{tour.id}.html' containing a self-contained, dark-themed responsive HTML page with embedded CSS. The page includes a grid layout of step cards with circular step-number badges, tour metadata, and an optional CTA button/link. HTML special characters in tour content are escaped. The file is text/html MIME type.
assertions.precondition: At least one tour is in the saved tours catalog

groups.name: Help Tab Integration
groups.description: The Product Tours feature also appears as a sub-tab in the Help section of the runner, accessible at the 'Product Tours' tab (MapPin icon). This view reads from the same instanceStorage key and supports playback and export. It serves as a launcher for tours discovered elsewhere in the app.

assertions.description: When no tours have been generated, the Help > Product Tours tab shows an empty state message: 'No tours generated yet. Go to Build > Product Tours to generate tours from page specs.' The message references the exact navigation path the user should follow.

target.label: Empty state message in Help tab

assertions.precondition: User is on the Help > Product Tours sub-tab and no tours are saved

assertions.description: The Help > Product Tours tab shows the description 'Interactive tours that demonstrate features automatically' beneath the section header

criteria.textContent: Interactive tours that demonstrate features automatically

target.label: Product Tours description in Help tab

assertions.precondition: User is on the Help > Product Tours sub-tab

assertions.description: When tours exist in instanceStorage, the Help > Product Tours tab displays them grouped by the same audience categories as the main page ('Getting Started', 'Power Features', 'Product Overview'). Tours support playback via TourPlayer and export via the same three format buttons. The Help tab and the main Product Tours page share the same instanceStorage data source — saving a tour on the main page makes it immediately visible on the Help tab.
assertions.precondition: At least one tour is saved and user is on the Help > Product Tours sub-tab

states.name: Idle — Ready to Generate
states.description: Default state on page load. The spec selector, audience dropdown, and 'Generate Tour' button are visible. No status messages, no preview, no Reset button.

transitions.name: Start generation
transitions.description: Select a spec, then click 'Generate Tour' to start AI generation

states.name: Generating — AI Request In-Flight
states.description: AI generation is in progress. A spinner and 'Generating tour(s) with AI...' text are visible. A 'Reset' button is visible in the header.

transitions.name: Generation completed
transitions.description: Automatically transitions when the AI response is received and parsed

transitions.name: Generation failed
transitions.description: Automatically transitions when the AI request fails or response cannot be parsed

states.name: Previewing — Tours Ready to Review
states.description: Generation succeeded. 'Preview' heading and TourCard grid are visible. 'Save N Tour(s)' and 'Regenerate' buttons are shown. 'Reset' is visible in the header.

transitions.name: Save tours
transitions.description: Click 'Save N Tour(s)' to persist the previewed tours to storage

transitions.name: Play preview tour
transitions.description: Click 'Start Tour' on a preview card to open TourPlayer while keeping the preview page visible

states.name: Done — Tours Saved
states.description: Tours were saved successfully. A green success message 'N tour(s) saved' is visible. The 'Generate Tour' button is available for a new generation. 'Reset' is visible in the header.

transitions.name: Reset page
transitions.description: Click 'Reset' to return to the idle state

transitions.name: Generate new tours
transitions.description: Click 'Generate Tour' again from the done state to start a fresh generation

states.name: Error — Generation Failed
states.description: AI generation failed. An error message in a red-bordered box is visible with an AlertCircle icon. 'Generate Tour' and 'Reset' buttons are available.

transitions.name: Retry generation
transitions.description: Click 'Generate Tour' to retry after an error

transitions.name: Reset after error
transitions.description: Click 'Reset' to dismiss the error and return to idle

states.name: Tour Playing — TourPlayer Active
states.description: TourPlayer overlay is open in the bottom-right corner. The background page remains visible. Navigation buttons (Back/Next/Finish), progress dots, and step content are shown.

transitions.name: Close TourPlayer
transitions.description: Click the X close button on TourPlayer to dismiss it and return to the background page state
